Question 3

Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial P4(x) of 11−3x about x=0.
P4(x)=1+3x+
9x2+27x3
+81x4

EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=0, so P4(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)2!x2+f‴(0)3!x3+f(4)(0)4!x4.

So we need to work out f(0), f′(0), f″(0), f‴(0) and f(4)(0), as follows: f(x)=11−3x=(1−3x)−1⟹f(0)=1f′(x)=3(1−3x)−2⟹f′(0)=3f″(x)=18(1−3x)−3⟹f″(0)=18f‴(x)=162(1−3x)−4⟹f‴(0)=162f(4)(x)=1944(1−3x)−5⟹f(4)(0)=1944

Therefore, P4(x) is given by P4(x)=1+(3)⋅x+182!x2+1623!x3+19444!x4=1+3x+9x2+27x3+81x4.
